title: Identification of small molecule inhibitors of Ebola virus by use of a biologically contained virus system.
abstract: Ebola virus disease is a severe illness with high mortality for which limited therapeutic options are available. Identifying new antiviral drugs that target viral proteins is essential for improving prevention and treatment strategies. In this study, we screened a library of 2,620 small molecules enriched for reported inhibitory activity against cellular and viral helicases to identify phenotypic inhibitors of a biologically contained virus, Ebola∆VP30 virus, in Vero cells stably expressing VP30 protein. Seven compounds significantly reduced virus titers at least 100-fold with minimal cytotoxicity and demonstrated low IC 50 values. Two of these compounds completely inhibited EbolaΔVP30 virus infection, interfering with either virus entry or replication. Although these preliminary screening hits require further optimization and in vivo validation, their identification opens new avenues for anti-Ebola virus drug discovery.

abstract_zh: 埃博拉病毒病 是一种 死亡率 较高的严重疾病,可用的治疗选择有限。识别针对病毒蛋白的新 抗病毒药物 药物对于改善预防和 治疗 策略至关重要。在这项研究中,我们筛选了一个包含 2,620 个小分子的文库,这些小分子富含报道的针对细胞和病毒解旋酶的抑制活性,以鉴定稳定表达 VP30 蛋白的 Vero 细胞中生物包含的病毒(埃博拉ΔVP30 病毒)的表型抑制剂。七种化合物显着降低病毒滴度至少 100 倍,且细胞毒性最小,并且 IC 50 值较低。其中两种化合物完全抑制埃博拉ΔVP30病毒感染,干扰病毒进入或复制。尽管这些初步筛选的命中需要进一步优化和体内验证,但它们的鉴定为抗 埃博拉病毒 药物发现开辟了新途径。

title: Structure and antigenicity of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus glycoprotein
abstract: An outbreak of ebolavirus disease caused by a new zoonotic spillover of Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) is currently spreading at an unprecedented pace in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. The outbreak has resulted in 7,733 cases with a case-fatality ratio of 48%, yet no BDBV-specific vaccines or therapeutics are available. The ebolavirus glycoprotein (GP) promotes viral entry and is the target of neutralizing antibodies and vaccine development. Here, we engineered a soluble, prefusion-stabilized GP trimer from a contemporary BDBV isolate and determined its cryo-electron microscopy structure bound to the broadly neutralizing antibody EBOV-515. It reveals the molecular basis for EBOV-515 cross-reactivity and suggests that the antibody inhibits viral entry by interfering with NPC1 engagement in addition to trapping GP in the prefusion conformation and hindering glycan cap cleavage. Mapping lineage-defining substitutions identified changes in GP1 and GP2, including R506S within an antigenic site targeted by multiple broadly neutralizing antibodies recognizing the fusion loop. Nevertheless, we found that several glycan cap-, GP base-, and HR2-directed antibodies cross-reacted and neutralized BDBV DRC/2026 GP pseudovirus with potency comparable or greater to that observed against earlier BDBV isolates and the Zaire ebolavirus Makona/2024 isolate. These findings define the antigenic properties of contemporary BDBV GP and delineate conserved epitopes as ideal targets for antibody therapeutics and for the development of pan-ebolavirus vaccines.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to understand the structure and antigenicity of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus glycoprotein (GP) to inform vaccine and therapeutic development, given the ongoing outbreak and lack of specific treatments or vaccines.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the engineering of a soluble, prefusion-stabilized GP trimer from a contemporary BDBV isolate and its cryo-electron microscopy structure determination, bound to the broadly neutralizing antibody EBOV-515.
analysis.methods: The methods included the generation of a BDBV GP trimer, cryo-electron microscopy structure determination, and antibody binding analysis.
analysis.main_results: The study revealed the molecular basis for EBOV-515 cross-reactivity and identified several conserved epitopes in the GP that are targets for cross-reactive antibodies.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the antibody EBOV-515 inhibits viral entry by interfering with NPC1 engagement and trapping GP in the prefusion conformation, and that several antibodies cross-react and neutralize BDBV with potency comparable to earlier isolates.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings define the antigenic properties of contemporary BDBV GP and delineate conserved epitopes as ideal targets for antibody therapeutics and pan-ebolavirus vaccines.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of a single contemporary BDBV isolate and the need for further validation in different isolates and settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study determined the structure and antigenicity of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus glycoprotein to inform vaccine and therapeutic development, revealing conserved epitopes as potential targets.

title_zh: 2026 Bundibugyo 病毒糖蛋白的结构和抗原性
source_body_en: An outbreak of ebolavirus disease caused by a new zoonotic spillover of Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) is currently spreading at an unprecedented pace in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. The outbreak has resulted in 7,733 cases with a case-fatality ratio of 48%, yet no BDBV-specific vaccines or therapeutics are available. The ebolavirus glycoprotein (GP) promotes viral entry and is the target of neutralizing antibodies and vaccine development. Here, we engineered a soluble, prefusion-stabilized GP trimer from a contemporary BDBV isolate and determined its cryo-electron microscopy structure bound to the broadly neutralizing antibody EBOV-515. It reveals the molecular basis for EBOV-515 cross-reactivity and suggests that the antibody inhibits viral entry by interfering with NPC1 engagement in addition to trapping GP in the prefusion conformation and hindering glycan cap cleavage. Mapping lineage-defining substitutions identified changes in GP1 and GP2, including R506S within an antigenic site targeted by multiple broadly neutralizing antibodies recognizing the fusion loop. Nevertheless, we found that several glycan cap-, GP base-, and HR2-directed antibodies cross-reacted and neutralized BDBV DRC/2026 GP pseudovirus with potency comparable or greater to that observed against earlier BDBV isolates and the Zaire ebolavirus Makona/2024 isolate. These findings define the antigenic properties of contemporary BDBV GP and delineate conserved epitopes as ideal targets for antibody therapeutics and for the development of pan-ebolavirus vaccines.

title: Epidemic response performance in contested territory: a comparative analysis of Ituri and North Kivu during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak
abstract: Abstract Background. The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is unfolding across provinces under materially different governance and security conditions. Ituri, the outbreak's epicentre, remains under national government administration despite insecurity; North Kivu's capital, Goma, and surrounding territory have been under March 23 Movement (M23)/Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC) control since early 2025. Existing published accounts treat insecurity as a generic, undifferentiated risk factor rather than isolating the specific contribution of contested territorial control. We compared Ituri and North Kivu on cumulative case fatality, health-zone coverage, and contact-tracing completeness using published, province-disaggregated surveillance figures from WHO, ECDC, and Africa CDC, contextualised against the documented conflict-related disruption of DRC's tenth Ebola outbreak (2018–2020), which affected the same two provinces. Two-proportion z-tests with 95% confidence intervals were used to test whether observed differences exceeded what chance alone would produce; the analysis is presented as hypothesis-generating throughout, consistent with the limits of an ecological design. As of 7–8 August 2026, Ituri had reported 3,636 confirmed cases and 1,551 deaths (case fatality 42.7%) across 28 of 36 health zones; North Kivu had reported 470 cases and 315 deaths (case fatality 67.0%) across 12 of 34 health zones. North Kivu's contact-tracing follow-up (74.7%) fell below both the national figure (79.2%) and the 90–95% interruption threshold. The outbreak reached 1,000 confirmed cases within 40 days of response activation, versus approximately 235 days for the 2018 outbreak in the same geography. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the impact of contested territorial control on epidemic response performance during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study compared the epidemic response performance in Ituri and North Kivu provinces, which were under different governance and security conditions during the outbreak. Ituri remained under national government administration, while North Kivu's capital and surrounding areas were under M23/AFC control since early 2025.
analysis.methods: The researchers used published, province-disaggregated surveillance figures from WHO, ECDC, and Africa CDC to compare cumulative case fatality, health-zone coverage, and contact-tracing completeness between Ituri and North Kivu. They applied two-proportion z-tests with 95% confidence intervals to assess whether observed differences were statistically significant.
analysis.main_results: As of 7–8 August 2026, Ituri reported 3,636 confirmed cases and 1,551 deaths (case fatality 42.7%) across 28 of 36 health zones, while North Kivu reported 470 cases and 315 deaths (case fatality 67.0%) across 12 of 34 health zones. North Kivu's contact-tracing follow-up (74.7%) was below the national figure (79.2%) and the 90–95% interruption threshold.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as highlighting the significant impact of governance and security conditions on epidemic response effectiveness, noting a marked case-fatality gap between the two provinces. This analysis is novel in its focus on the specific contribution of contested territorial control to outbreak dynamics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform public health strategies by emphasizing the need for tailored epidemic response approaches in regions with varying governance and security contexts, particularly in conflict-affected areas.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its ecological design and reliance on published surveillance figures, which may not capture all nuances of local response efforts. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these constraints.

analysis.summary_en: This study compares the epidemic response performance during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in Ituri and North Kivu provinces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Ituri, under national government control, reported 3,636 confirmed cases and 1,551 deaths (case fatality 42.7%) across 28 health zones, while North Kivu, under M23/AFC control, reported 470 cases and 315 deaths (case fatality 67.0%) across 12 health zones. The authors highlight the significant case-fatality gap and note that North Kivu's contact-tracing follow-up fell below national standards. They interpret these differences as stemming from the impact of governance and security conditions on outbreak response. The study's findings suggest that tailored public health strategies are necessary in conflict-affected regions. However, the ecological design and reliance on published surveillance data limit the strength of the evidence, which is considered moderate.

source_body_en: Abstract Background. The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is unfolding across provinces under materially different governance and security conditions. Ituri, the outbreak's epicentre, remains under national government administration despite insecurity; North Kivu's capital, Goma, and surrounding territory have been under March 23 Movement (M23)/Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC) control since early 2025. Existing published accounts treat insecurity as a generic, undifferentiated risk factor rather than isolating the specific contribution of contested territorial control. We compared Ituri and North Kivu on cumulative case fatality, health-zone coverage, and contact-tracing completeness using published, province-disaggregated surveillance figures from WHO, ECDC, and Africa CDC, contextualised against the documented conflict-related disruption of DRC's tenth Ebola outbreak (2018–2020), which affected the same two provinces. North Kivu's contact-tracing follow-up (74.7%) fell below both the national figure (79.2%) and the 90–95% interruption threshold. The outbreak reached 1,000 confirmed cases within 40 days of response activation, versus approximately 235 days for the 2018 outbreak in the same geography. title: Filovirus Seroreactivity Beyond Virus-Specific Outbreak Regions in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2015-2023
abstract: ABSTRACT The ongoing Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is the second-largest Ebola disease outbreak in recorded history, and only the second recorded BVD outbreak in the country. While the DRC has recorded 18 filovirus disease outbreaks, the historical frequency and geographic distribution of human filovirus exposures remain poorly understood. Using a multiplexed multi-filovirus immunoassay, we assessed antibody reactivity against antigens of filoviruses linked to human disease, Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), Ebola virus (EBOV), Marburg virus (MARV), and Sudan virus (SUDV), among eleven cohorts from seven provinces between 2015–2023 (n=5,852). Participants with median fluorescence intensity values exceeding established antigen-specific cutoffs were classified as seroreactive. Seroreactivity against glycoprotein (GP) targets of all four viruses were detected in every cohort, demonstrating evidence of filovirus or an antigenically related exposure well beyond known outbreak regions. Seroreactivity estimates varied by cohort site, with 60.8% of participants (n=175/288) in Mongala Province in April 2016 considered seroreactive against BDBV GP. In this cohort, 4.2%, 29.9%, and 34.7% of participants were seroreactive against EBOV, MARV and SUDV GP, respectively yet only 1.7% were seroreactive against all four GP antigens. In adjusted analyses, site was the primary predictor of seroreactivity, with odds for BDBV seroreactivity 9.1-fold (95%CI 7.0-11.9) and 9.5-fold (95%CI 6.9-13.2) higher in Mongala and Tshuapa provinces than in Kwilu. Similarly, the adjusted odds of MARV and SUDV GP seroreactivity were 4.5-fold and 7.1-fold higher in Mongala, and 3.7-fold and 6.1-fold higher in Tshuapa, than Kwilu. Among 280 individuals sampled longitudinally, BDBV GP detected seroconversion was comparable by site, with 12.8% in Kwilu and 10.4% in Mongala having detected seroreactivity three and five years after initial contact, respectively. Overall, these results indicate widespread, geographically heterogeneous filovirus seroreactivity across sampled cohorts. These findings may reflect zoonotic spillover events, leading to undetected human-to-human filovirus circulation, including paucisymptomatic or asymptomatic infections, or exposure to as-yet unidentified antigenically cross-reactive viruses. These data highlight gaps in understanding the historical and geographic distribution of filovirus exposure in the DRC and support further prospective serological, epidemiological, and molecular investigations, especially given the current outbreak.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 刚果民主共和国(DRC)正在发生的本迪布焦病毒病(BVD)ZX​​QTERMXQXZ是有记录以来第二大埃博拉病毒病暴发,也是该国仅有第二记录的BVD 暴发。尽管刚果民主共和国已记录了 18 种丝状病毒疾病 暴发,但人类丝状病毒暴露的历史频率和地理分布仍知之甚少。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用多重多丝状病毒免疫测定,我们评估了 2015 年至 2023 年间来自七个省的 11 个 队列研究 中与人类疾病相关的丝状病毒、本迪布焦病毒 (BDBV)、埃博拉病毒 (EBOV)、马尔堡病毒 (MARV) 和苏丹病毒 (SUDV) 抗原的抗体反应性 (n=5,852)。
elements_zh.methods: 荧光强度中值超过既定抗原特异性截止值的参与者被归类为血清反应性。血清反应性估计因 队列研究 站点而异,2016 年 4 月蒙加拉省 60.8% 的参与者 (n=175/288) 被认为对 BDBV GP 有血清反应性。在该 队列研究 中,分别有 4.2%、29.9% 和 34.7% 的参与者对 EBOV、MARV 和 SUDV GP 呈血清反应,但只有 1.7% 对所有四种 GP 抗原呈血清反应。
elements_zh.main_results: 在每个 队列研究 中均检测到所有四种病毒针对糖蛋白 (GP) 靶标的血清反应性,证明丝状病毒或抗原相关暴露的证据远远超出已知的 暴发 区域。在调整后的分析中,地点是血清反应性的主要预测因素,蒙加拉省和楚阿帕省的 BDBV 血清反应性几率比奎卢省高 9.1 倍(95% CI 7.0-11.9)和 9.5 倍(95% CI 6.9-13.2)。同样,Mongala 地区 MARV 和 SUDV GP 血清反应性的调整后赔率比 Kwilu 地区高 4.5 倍和 7.1 倍,Tshuapa 地区高 3.7 倍和 6.1 倍。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现可能反映了人畜共患的 跨物种溢出 事件,导致未检测到的人际丝状病毒传播,包括少症状或无症状感染,或暴露于尚未鉴定的抗原交叉反应病毒。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果表明 队列研究 样本中存在广泛的、地理异质的丝状病毒血清反应性。这些数据凸显了在了解刚果民主共和国丝状病毒暴露的历史和地理分布方面的差距,并支持进一步的前瞻性血清学、流行病学和分子研究,特别是考虑到当前的 暴发。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据没有报告任何随机化或盲法,这可能会引入偏差。研究设计的局限性和缺乏比较组降低了证据的强度。

analysis_zh.methods: 荧光强度中值超过既定抗原特异性截止值的参与者被归类为血清反应性。血清反应性估计因 队列研究 站点而异,2016 年 4 月蒙加拉省 60.8% 的参与者 (n=175/288) 被认为对 BDBV GP 有血清反应性。在该 队列研究 中,分别有 4.2%、29.9% 和 34.7% 的参与者对 EBOV、MARV 和 SUDV GP 呈血清反应,但只有 1.7% 对所有四种 GP 抗原呈血清反应。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在每个 队列研究 中均检测到所有四种病毒针对糖蛋白 (GP) 靶标的血清反应性,证明丝状病毒或抗原相关暴露的证据远远超出已知的 暴发 区域。在调整后的分析中,地点是血清反应性的主要预测因素,蒙加拉省和楚阿帕省的 BDBV 血清反应性几率比奎卢省高 9.1 倍(95% CI 7.0-11.9)和 9.5 倍(95% CI 6.9-13.2)。同样,Mongala 地区 MARV 和 SUDV GP 血清反应性的调整后赔率比 Kwilu 地区高 4.5 倍和 7.1 倍,Tshuapa 地区高 3.7 倍和 6.1 倍。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现可能反映了人畜共患的 跨物种溢出 事件,导致未检测到的人际丝状病毒传播,包括少症状或无症状感染,或暴露于尚未鉴定的抗原交叉反应病毒。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果表明 队列研究 样本中存在广泛的、地理异质的丝状病毒血清反应性。这些数据凸显了在了解刚果民主共和国丝状病毒暴露的历史和地理分布方面的差距,并支持进一步的前瞻性血清学、流行病学和分子研究,特别是考虑到当前的 暴发。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据没有报告任何随机化或盲法,这可能会引入偏差。研究设计的局限性和缺乏比较组降低了证据的强度。

title: Bundibugyo virus disease and military health facilities in Nigeria: a rapid review of clinical, diagnostic and countermeasure evidence and surveillance integration gaps.
abstract: This project is a rapid review of the evidence on Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) and its implications for military health facilities in Nigeria. Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) caused the largest Ebola disease epidemic ever recorded in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in May 2026, with onward cases in Uganda, Kenya, Europe and, on 20 October 2026, an imported case in Abuja, Nigeria. Ebola preparedness across Africa was built around a different species, Zaire ebolavirus: the licensed vaccine, the licensed monoclonal antibody therapies and the most widely deployed near-patient diagnostic assay all target that species, and none is approved for BDBV. The review has two purposes. The first is to consolidate current evidence on BDBV virology, clinical features, diagnosis, treatment, vaccines and infection prevention, as of late October 2026. The second is to examine how Nigerian military health facilities connect to the national Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (IDSR) system. These facilities serve internationally deployed personnel, their families and often civilian patients, but report through a separate command chain, and no published study has measured their surveillance reporting. Methods follow Cochrane Rapid Reviews Methods Group guidance, reported using PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S. Searches of PubMed, Europe PMC, HAL, African Journals Online and ClinicalTrials.gov were run on 24 October 2026, supplemented by WHO, Africa CDC, ECDC, US CDC, Nigerian government and United Nations sources. Screening is by one reviewer with second-reviewer verification, and synthesis is narrative. Expected outcomes are a current synthesis of BDBV evidence for clinicians and public health staff in West Africa, a description of how military health facilities sit relative to national surveillance in Nigeria, and a set of preparedness priorities for those facilities covering surveillance connection, screening of returning personnel, case definitions, laboratory pathways, isolation readiness, joint contact tracing and trial access. A further expected outcome is documentation of an evidence gap: preliminary searching found no study measuring IDSR reporting from Nigerian military facilities. If confirmed, that absence is itself a finding, and the review will propose a facility-level assessment as the priority next study. The search strategy, record list, screening decisions and literature matrix will be deposited with this project. The protocol was registered after the searches and a first pass of title and abstract screening, but before full-text screening, data extraction and synthesis; no protocol was registered prospectively.

title_zh: 尼日利亚本迪布焦病毒病和军事卫生设施:对临床、诊断和对策证据以及 监测 整合差距的快速审查。
source_body_en: This project is a rapid review of the evidence on Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) and its implications for military health facilities in Nigeria. Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) caused the largest Ebola disease epidemic ever recorded in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in May 2026, with onward cases in Uganda, Kenya, Europe and, on 20 October 2026, an imported case in Abuja, Nigeria. Ebola preparedness across Africa was built around a different species, Zaire ebolavirus: the licensed vaccine, the licensed monoclonal antibody therapies and the most widely deployed near-patient diagnostic assay all target that species, and none is approved for BDBV. The review has two purposes. The first is to consolidate current evidence on BDBV virology, clinical features, diagnosis, treatment, vaccines and infection prevention, as of late October 2026. The second is to examine how Nigerian military health facilities connect to the national Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (IDSR) system. These facilities serve internationally deployed personnel, their families and often civilian patients, but report through a separate command chain, and no published study has measured their surveillance reporting. Methods follow Cochrane Rapid Reviews Methods Group guidance, reported using PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S. Searches of PubMed, Europe PMC, HAL, African Journals Online and ClinicalTrials.gov were run on 24 October 2026, supplemented by WHO, Africa CDC, ECDC, US CDC, Nigerian government and United Nations sources. Screening is by one reviewer with second-reviewer verification, and synthesis is narrative. Expected outcomes are a current synthesis of BDBV evidence for clinicians and public health staff in West Africa, a description of how military health facilities sit relative to national surveillance in Nigeria, and a set of preparedness priorities for those facilities covering surveillance connection, screening of returning personnel, case definitions, laboratory pathways, isolation readiness, joint contact tracing and trial access. A further expected outcome is documentation of an evidence gap: preliminary searching found no study measuring IDSR reporting from Nigerian military facilities. If confirmed, that absence is itself a finding, and the review will propose a facility-level assessment as the priority next study. The search strategy, record list, screening decisions and literature matrix will be deposited with this project. The protocol was registered after the searches and a first pass of title and abstract screening, but before full-text screening, data extraction and synthesis; no protocol was registered prospectively.

title: Immunologic and placental responses to the VSV-EBOV vaccine in a pregnant mouse model.
abstract: Ebola virus disease is a severe viral hemorrhagic illness with high maternal and perinatal mortality. Although the replication-competent vesicular stomatitis virus-based Ebola vaccine (VSV-EBOV) has been deployed successfully in outbreak settings, pregnant women were excluded from clinical trials, leaving critical safety gaps. To address this, we developed a murine model to assess pregnancy outcomes following VSV-EBOV exposure at different gestational stages. Pregnant C57BL/6 mice vaccinated at embryonic day 7 (E7), E10, or E15 mounted robust anti-Ebola virus (anti-EBOV) antibody responses comparable to those of non-pregnant controls and efficiently cleared the vaccine virus without evidence of vertical transmission. However, peri-implantation vaccination modestly increased fetal resorption and early postnatal mortality, accompanied by placental pathology characterized by vascular remodeling defects and inflammation. Later gestational vaccination had minimal impact on survival or offspring development. Mechanistic studies revealed that these adverse effects were mediated by type I interferon signaling rather than direct viral infection, as IFN-β-deficient mice exhibited normal pregnancy outcomes and blocking interferon receptor activity ameliorated placental pathology despite higher viral loads. To our knowledge, these findings represent the first comprehensive preclinical safety evaluation of VSV-EBOV vaccination during pregnancy and identify a critical window of vulnerability early in gestation. More broadly, this work underscores the central role of interferons in shaping placental immune responses and provides an experimental framework to guide evaluation of live-virus vaccines in pregnancy.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the safety and immunologic responses of the VSV-EBOV vaccine in a pregnant mouse model. The research addresses the critical safety gaps in vaccine trials for pregnant women, as they were excluded from clinical studies. Using a murine model, the study evaluates pregnancy outcomes following vaccination at different gestational stages. Results show that vaccination during early pregnancy leads to increased fetal resorption and placental pathology, while later vaccination has minimal impact. Mechanistic studies suggest that these effects are mediated by type I interferon signaling rather than direct viral infection. The findings provide important insights into the safety of live-virus vaccines during pregnancy and highlight the role of interferons in placental immune responses. The study's results are based on direct observations in a controlled experimental setting, offering a preclinical framework for future research. However, the study is limited to a murine model, which may not fully translate to human outcomes.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 埃博拉病毒病 是一种严重的病毒性出血性疾病,孕产妇和围产儿 死亡率 发病率较高。尽管基于水泡性口炎病毒的埃博拉 疫苗 (VSV-EBOV) 已在 暴发 环境中成功部署,但孕妇被排除在临床试验之外,从而留下了严重的安全漏洞。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 为了解决这个问题,我们开发了一种小鼠模型来评估不同妊娠阶段暴露于 VSV-EBOV 后的妊娠结局。
elements_zh.methods: 在胚胎第 7 天 (E7)、E10 或 E15 接种疫苗的怀孕 C57BL/6 小鼠产生了与非怀孕对照相当的强大抗 埃博拉病毒(抗 EBOV)抗体反应,并有效清除了 疫苗 病毒,而没有垂直 传播 的证据。
elements_zh.main_results: 然而,围植入期 疫苗接种 适度增加胎儿吸收和产后早期 死亡率,并伴有以血管重塑缺陷和炎症为特征的胎盘病理。

title_zh: 怀孕小鼠模型中 VSV-EBOV 疫苗 的免疫学和胎盘反应。
source_body_en: Ebola virus disease is a severe viral hemorrhagic illness with high maternal and perinatal mortality. Although the replication-competent vesicular stomatitis virus-based Ebola vaccine (VSV-EBOV) has been deployed successfully in outbreak settings, pregnant women were excluded from clinical trials, leaving critical safety gaps. To address this, we developed a murine model to assess pregnancy outcomes following VSV-EBOV exposure at different gestational stages. Pregnant C57BL/6 mice vaccinated at embryonic day 7 (E7), E10, or E15 mounted robust anti-Ebola virus (anti-EBOV) antibody responses comparable to those of non-pregnant controls and efficiently cleared the vaccine virus without evidence of vertical transmission. However, peri-implantation vaccination modestly increased fetal resorption and early postnatal mortality, accompanied by placental pathology characterized by vascular remodeling defects and inflammation. Later gestational vaccination had minimal impact on survival or offspring development. Mechanistic studies revealed that these adverse effects were mediated by type I interferon signaling rather than direct viral infection, as IFN-β-deficient mice exhibited normal pregnancy outcomes and blocking interferon receptor activity ameliorated placental pathology despite higher viral loads. To our knowledge, these findings represent the first comprehensive preclinical safety evaluation of VSV-EBOV vaccination during pregnancy and identify a critical window of vulnerability early in gestation. More broadly, this work underscores the central role of interferons in shaping placental immune responses and provides an experimental framework to guide evaluation of live-virus vaccines in pregnancy.
abstract_zh: 埃博拉病毒病 是一种严重的病毒性出血性疾病,孕产妇和围产儿 死亡率 发病率较高。尽管基于水泡性口炎病毒的埃博拉 疫苗 (VSV-EBOV) 已在 暴发 环境中成功部署,但孕妇被排除在临床试验之外,从而留下了严重的安全漏洞。为了解决这个问题,我们开发了一种小鼠模型来评估不同妊娠阶段暴露于 VSV-EBOV 后的妊娠结局。在胚胎第 7 天 (E7)、E10 或 E15 接种疫苗的怀孕 C57BL/6 小鼠产生了与非怀孕对照相当的强大抗 埃博拉病毒(抗 EBOV)抗体反应,并有效清除了 疫苗 病毒,而没有垂直 传播 的证据。然而,围植入期 疫苗接种 适度增加胎儿吸收和产后早期 死亡率,并伴有以血管重塑缺陷和炎症为特征的胎盘病理。妊娠后期 疫苗接种 对生存或后代发育的影响很小。机制研究表明,这些不良反应是由 I 型干扰素信号传导而非直接病毒感染介导的,因为 IFN-β 缺陷小鼠表现出正常妊娠结局,并且尽管病毒载量较高,但阻断干扰素受体活性可改善胎盘病理。据我们所知,这些研究结果代表了 VSV-EBOV 疫苗接种 在怀孕期间的首次全面临床前安全性评估,并确定了妊娠早期脆弱性的关键窗口。更广泛地说,这项工作强调了干扰素在塑造胎盘 免疫应答 中的核心作用,并提供了一个实验框架来指导妊娠期活病毒 疫苗 的评估。

title: SARS, H1N1, EBOLA, COVID-19, MPOX, H5N1 AND HANTAVIRUS: IS HUMANITY ENTERING A NEW ERA OF PANDEMIC? IS TÜRKİYE PREPARED FOR THE NEXT GLOBAL OUTBREAK?
abstract: The emergence and re-emergence of infectious diseases pose persistent challenges to global health security. Outbreaks such as severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), influenza A(H1N1), Ebola virus disease, coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), mpox, avian influenza A(H5N1), and hantavirus infections highlight the need for effective preparedness against emerging infectious threats. The concept of “Disease X” further emphasizes the importance of preparing for unknown pathogens that may cause future epidemics or pandemics. This study aimed to examine major infectious disease outbreaks and assess Türkiye’s preparedness for potential future global outbreaks. A descriptive review design was employed, based on a structured literature search and document analysis of scientific publications and institutional reports. The findings were organized and interpreted using a SWOT framework. The analysis identified healthcare infrastructure, intensive care capacity, digital health systems, and experience gained during the COVID-19 pandemic as potential strengths. However, challenges related to healthcare workforce capacity, zoonotic disease surveillance, public health literacy, coordination across human, animal, and environmental health sectors, and dependence on external sources for certain biotechnological products may constrain preparedness. Climate change, environmental disruption, international travel, migration, and global trade were identified as factors that may influence the emergence and spread of infectious diseases. Strengthening integrated surveillance and early warning systems, improving intersectoral coordination through the One Health approach, enhancing domestic vaccine and diagnostic production capacity, and expanding community-based public health education may help improve Türkiye’s preparedness for future outbreaks. These findings highlight the importance of sustained, multisectoral preparedness for emerging infectious disease threats.
journal: International Journal of Health Services Research and Policy

analysis.summary_en: This review article examines the emergence and re-emergence of infectious diseases, with a focus on Ebola viruses and Türkiye’s preparedness for future outbreaks. It highlights the persistent challenges posed by these diseases and outlines the strengths and weaknesses of Türkiye’s current systems. source_body_en: The emergence and re-emergence of infectious diseases pose persistent challenges to global health security. Outbreaks such as severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), influenza A(H1N1), Ebola virus disease, coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), mpox, avian influenza A(H5N1), and hantavirus infections highlight the need for effective preparedness against emerging infectious threats. The concept of “Disease X” further emphasizes the importance of preparing for unknown pathogens that may cause future epidemics or pandemics. This study aimed to examine major infectious disease outbreaks and assess Türkiye’s preparedness for potential future global outbreaks. A descriptive review design was employed, based on a structured literature search and document analysis of scientific publications and institutional reports. The findings were organized and interpreted using a SWOT framework. The analysis identified healthcare infrastructure, intensive care capacity, digital health systems, and experience gained during the COVID-19 pandemic as potential strengths. However, challenges related to healthcare workforce capacity, zoonotic disease surveillance, public health literacy, coordination across human, animal, and environmental health sectors, and dependence on external sources for certain biotechnological products may constrain preparedness. Climate change, environmental disruption, international travel, migration, and global trade were identified as factors that may influence the emergence and spread of infectious diseases. Strengthening integrated surveillance and early warning systems, improving intersectoral coordination through the One Health approach, enhancing domestic vaccine and diagnostic production capacity, and expanding community-based public health education may help improve Türkiye’s preparedness for future outbreaks. These findings highlight the importance of sustained, multisectoral preparedness for emerging infectious disease threats.

title: Actin remodeling by human RNA virus: mechanisms and targeted intervention
abstract: The actin cytoskeleton is a central dynamic network in eukaryotic cells which preserves morphology, motility, and intracellular transport. Extensive research has confirmed the importance of actin in RNA viral infection. Actin remodeling, as a core host mechanism exploited by RNA viruses, strongly affects viral replication and transmission efficiency. This article reviews the key regulatory molecules involved in actin dynamics. Based on this foundation, we focus on recent advances in the molecular mechanisms by which six representative human RNA viruses(severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2, influenza A virus, respiratory syncytial virus, dengue virus, ebola virus and human immunodeficiency virus) hijack the host actin network, revealing the actin hijacking pathways that RNA viruses tend to select. Finally, we further summarize the current status of research on antiviral compounds that target the actin signaling pathway. Given that targeting host factors offers the unique advantage of broad-spectrum antiviral activity, this strategy offers promise for overcoming drug resistance caused by high viral mutation rates. However, its clinical application still faces difficulties in balancing cytotoxicity and efficacy. This article intends to provide a conceptual framework for novel antiviral intervention approaches targeting actin.
journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 肌动蛋白细胞骨架是真核细胞中的中央动态网络,它保留形态、运动性和细胞内运输。广泛的研究已经证实肌动蛋白在RNA病毒感染中的重要性。肌动蛋白重塑作为RNA病毒利用的核心宿主机制,强烈影响病毒复制和传播效率。本文综述了肌动蛋白动力学中涉及的关键调控分子,重点介绍了六种代表性人类RNA病毒劫持宿主肌动蛋白网络的分子机制的最新进展,揭示了RNA病毒倾向于选择的肌动蛋白劫持途径。最后,文章总结了针对肌动蛋白信号通路的抗病毒药物化合物的研究现状。

elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 鉴于针对 宿主 因子在平衡细胞毒性和功效方面仍然面临困难,这代表了具体的证据差距。靶向肌动蛋白信号通路进行抗病毒药物干预的临床应用仍面临挑战。

title_zh: 人类RNA病毒对肌动蛋白的重塑:机制和靶向干预
source_body_en: The actin cytoskeleton is a central dynamic network in eukaryotic cells which preserves morphology, motility, and intracellular transport. Extensive research has confirmed the importance of actin in RNA viral infection. Actin remodeling, as a core host mechanism exploited by RNA viruses, strongly affects viral replication and transmission efficiency. This article reviews the key regulatory molecules involved in actin dynamics. Based on this foundation, we focus on recent advances in the molecular mechanisms by which six representative human RNA viruses(severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2, influenza A virus, respiratory syncytial virus, dengue virus, ebola virus and human immunodeficiency virus) hijack the host actin network, revealing the actin hijacking pathways that RNA viruses tend to select. Finally, we further summarize the current status of research on antiviral compounds that target the actin signaling pathway. Given that targeting host factors offers the unique advantage of broad-spectrum antiviral activity, this strategy offers promise for overcoming drug resistance caused by high viral mutation rates. However, its clinical application still faces difficulties in balancing cytotoxicity and efficacy. This article intends to provide a conceptual framework for novel antiviral intervention approaches targeting actin.
abstract_zh: 肌动蛋白细胞骨架是真核细胞中一个核心的动态网络,负责维持细胞形态、运动性和细胞内运输。大量研究表明,肌动蛋白在RNA病毒感染中具有重要作用。肌动蛋白重塑作为RNA病毒利用的核心宿主机制,强烈影响病毒复制和传播效率。本文综述了参与肌动蛋白动态调控的关键调节分子。在此基础上,我们重点探讨了六种代表性的人类RNA病毒(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒-2、甲型流感病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒、登革病毒、埃博拉病毒和人类免疫缺陷病毒)如何劫持宿主肌动蛋白网络,揭示RNA病毒倾向于选择的肌动蛋白劫持途径。最后,我们进一步总结了当前针对抗病毒药物化合物作用于肌动蛋白信号通路的研究现状。鉴于针对宿主因子具有独特的广谱抗病毒药物活性优势,这种策略为克服高病毒突变率导致的耐药性提供了希望。然而,其临床应用仍面临平衡细胞毒性与疗效的困难。本文旨在为针对肌动蛋白的新型抗病毒药物干预方法提供概念框架。

title: Biocontainment Transport of Patients with High-Consequence Infectious Diseases: A Narrative Review and Integrated Operational Framework for Emergency Medical Systems
abstract: Background: /Objectives: The transport of patients with high-consequence infectious diseases (HCIDs) links biosafety science and emergency medicine. The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease epidemic and the multinational Andes virus outbreak associated with an expedition cruise ship have renewed attention on how such patients are moved safely between the community, hospitals and high-level isolation units. This narrative review synthesises the international literature on biocontainment transport and integrates it into an operational framework for emergency medical systems. Methods: A structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus (to 10 October 2026), complemented by guidance from the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and national authorities, was conducted and reported according to the SANRA scale. Evidence was organised across seven operational domains and combined with the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service. Results: Of 2432 records identified, 1485 unique records were screened. The literature is dominated by aeromedical case reports, technical evaluations and expert consensus, with few comparative studies. Recurrent findings concern device integrity and air quality within transport isolators, the risk of self-contamination during doffing, heat strain and communication limits imposed by personal protective equipment, decontamination of vehicles and isolators, the maintenance of team readiness during periods of low activity, and the psychological burden on patients and staff. These findings are integrated into a framework comprising a four-link containment chain, a seven-phase operational workflow, a three-tier complexity classification and a role-based responsibility matrix. Conclusions: Biocontainment transport is better understood as an integrated emergency system than as a device-centred intervention. The proposed framework is a structured, consensus-based reference for planning, training and quality assurance; its components require prospective evaluation.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the transport of patients with high-consequence infectious diseases (HCIDs), specifically examining biocontainment practices. The central question is how emergency medical systems can safely move patients infected with human-pathogenic orthoebolaviruses and related viruses, with an emphasis on operational frameworks and system integration.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus up to 10 October 2026, guided by the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and national authorities. The findings were reported according to the SANRA scale and integrated with the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The literature is dominated by aeromedical case reports, technical evaluations, and expert consensus, with few comparative studies. Recurrent findings include device integrity and air quality within transport isolators, the risk of self-contamination during doffing, heat strain, communication limits imposed by personal protective equipment, decontamination of vehicles and isolators, team readiness during low-activity periods, and the psychological burden on patients and staff. These findings are integrated into a framework comprising a four-link containment chain, a seven-phase operational workflow, a three-tier complexity classification, and a role-based responsibility matrix.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The literature lacks comparative studies and is dominated by case reports and expert consensus, which may limit the generalizability of findings. There is also a lack of prospective evaluation of the framework components, and the review notes that the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service was used to complement the evidence.

The components of the framework require prospective evaluation to validate their effectiveness. Additionally, the review highlights the need for further research on comparative studies and the operational challenges of biocontainment transport.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review explores the challenges and best practices in biocontainment transport for patients with high-consequence infectious diseases, focusing on human-pathogenic orthoebolaviruses. The review synthesizes international literature and integrates it into an operational framework for emergency medical systems. Key findings include recurring issues such as device integrity, self-contamination risks, heat strain, communication limitations, and psychological burdens. The framework includes a four-link containment chain, seven-phase workflow, three-tier complexity classification, and a role-based matrix. The review emphasizes the need for prospective evaluation of the framework components and highlights the lack of comparative studies in the literature. The implications suggest that biocontainment transport should be viewed as an integrated emergency system rather than a device-centered intervention.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该审查的重点是严重后果传染病(HCID)患者的运输,特别是检查生物防护实践。核心问题是紧急医疗系统如何安全地转移感染人类致病性正埃博拉病毒及相关病毒的患者,重点是操作框架和系统集成。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述在世界卫生组织、欧洲疾病预防和控制中心、美国疾病控制和预防中心以及国家当局的指导下,对截至 2026 年 10 月 10 日的 PubMed/MEDLINE 和 Scopus 进行了结构化检索。研究结果根据 SANRA 等级进行报告,并结合意大利红十字会生物防护运输服务的运营经验。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 文献以航空医学病例报告、技术评估、专家共识为主,比较研究较少。反复出现的调查结果包括运输隔离器内的设备完整性和空气质量、落纱过程中的自我污染风险、热应变、个人防护设备造成的通信限制、车辆和隔离器的净化、低活动期间的团队准备情况以及患者和工作人员的心理负担。这些发现被整合到一个框架中,该框架包括四链接遏制链、七阶段操作工作流程、三层复杂性分类和基于角色的责任矩阵。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 文献缺乏比较研究,且以病例报告和专家共识为主,这可能会限制研究结果的普遍性。还缺乏对框架组成部分的前瞻性评估,审查指出,意大利红十字会生物防护运输服务的运营经验被用来补充证据。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 拟议的框架是一个结构化的、基于共识的规划、培训和质量保证参考。该框架的组成部分需要进行前瞻性评估以验证其有效性。此外,该审查强调需要进一步研究比较研究和生物防护运输的操作挑战。

analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The proposed framework is a structured, consensus-based reference for planning, training, and quality assurance. The components of the framework require prospective evaluation to validate their effectiveness. title_zh: 严重后果传染病患者的生物防护运输:紧急医疗系统的叙述回顾和综合运营框架
source_body_en: Background: /Objectives: The transport of patients with high-consequence infectious diseases (HCIDs) links biosafety science and emergency medicine. The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease epidemic and the multinational Andes virus outbreak associated with an expedition cruise ship have renewed attention on how such patients are moved safely between the community, hospitals and high-level isolation units. This narrative review synthesises the international literature on biocontainment transport and integrates it into an operational framework for emergency medical systems. Methods: A structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus (to 10 October 2026), complemented by guidance from the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and national authorities, was conducted and reported according to the SANRA scale. Evidence was organised across seven operational domains and combined with the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service. Results: Of 2432 records identified, 1485 unique records were screened. The literature is dominated by aeromedical case reports, technical evaluations and expert consensus, with few comparative studies. Recurrent findings concern device integrity and air quality within transport isolators, the risk of self-contamination during doffing, heat strain and communication limits imposed by personal protective equipment, decontamination of vehicles and isolators, the maintenance of team readiness during periods of low activity, and the psychological burden on patients and staff. These findings are integrated into a framework comprising a four-link containment chain, a seven-phase operational workflow, a three-tier complexity classification and a role-based responsibility matrix. Conclusions: Biocontainment transport is better understood as an integrated emergency system than as a device-centred intervention. The proposed framework is a structured, consensus-based reference for planning, training and quality assurance; its components require prospective evaluation.
abstract_zh: 背景:/目标:严重后果传染病(HCID)患者的转运将生物安全科学和急诊医学联系在一起。2026年的本迪布焦病毒病疫情以及与一艘探险游轮相关的多国安第斯山脉病毒暴发再次引起人们对如何在社区、医院和高级隔离单位之间安全转移此类患者的关注。这篇叙述性综述综合了有关生物防护运输的国际文献,并将其整合到紧急医疗系统的操作框架中。方法:根据 SANRA 量表,对 PubMed/MEDLINE 和 Scopus(截至 2026 年 10 月 10 日)进行结构化检索,并辅以世界卫生组织、欧洲疾病预防和控制中心、美国疾病控制和预防中心以及国家当局的指导。证据跨七个业务领域进行组织,并结合意大利红十字会生物防护运输服务的运营经验。结果:在已识别的 2432 条记录中,筛选出 1485 条独特记录。文献以航空医学病例报告、技术评估和专家共识为主,比较研究较少。反复出现的调查结果涉及运输隔离器内的设备完整性和空气质量、落纱过程中的自我污染风险、个人防护设备造成的热应变和通信限制、车辆和隔离器的净化、低活动期间团队准备状态的保持以及患者和工作人员的心理负担。这些发现被整合到一个框架中,该框架包括四链接遏制链、七阶段操作工作流程、三层复杂性分类和基于角色的责任矩阵。结论:生物防护运输最好理解为一个综合应急系统,而不是一种以设备为中心的干预措施。拟议的框架是一个结构化的、基于共识的规划、培训和质量保证参考;其组成部分需要前瞻性评估。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该审查的重点是严重后果传染病(HCID)患者的运输,特别是检查生物防护实践。核心问题是紧急医疗系统如何安全地转移感染人类致病性正埃博拉病毒及相关病毒的患者,重点是操作框架和系统集成。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述在世界卫生组织、欧洲疾病预防和控制中心、美国疾病控制和预防中心以及国家当局的指导下,对截至 2026 年 10 月 10 日的 PubMed/MEDLINE 和 Scopus 进行了结构化检索。研究结果根据 SANRA 等级进行报告,并结合意大利红十字会生物防护运输服务的运营经验。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 文献以航空医学病例报告、技术评估、专家共识为主,比较研究较少。反复出现的调查结果包括运输隔离器内的设备完整性和空气质量、落纱过程中的自我污染风险、热应变、个人防护设备造成的通信限制、车辆和隔离器的净化、低活动期间的团队准备情况以及患者和工作人员的心理负担。这些发现被整合到一个框架中,该框架包括四链接遏制链、七阶段操作工作流程、三层复杂性分类和基于角色的责任矩阵。

title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Regarding Marburg Virus Disease Among Healthcare Workers in Dilla University Teaching Hospital, Ethiopia: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Background Healthcare workers are a first contact for patients with infectious diseases and may be at occupational risk during hemorrhagic fever outbreaks. The Marburg virus disease (MVD) outbreak in southern Ethiopia, ongoing during data collection in December 2025, highlighted the need to assess healthcare workers' knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding MVD. Therefore, this study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices and examined factors associated with practice among healthcare work. Methods A cross-sectional study of 238 healthcare workers at Dilla University Teaching Hospital was conducted from December 1 to December 22, 2025. Descriptive statistics, frequencies, and percentages summarized participant characteristics and KAP responses. Binary logistic regression examined factors associated with good practice. Variables with p value ≤ 0.25 in bivariable analysis were included in the multivariable model. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and significance was set at p Results About 51.7%, 57.1%, and 55.0% of participants had good knowledge, positive attitudes, and good practice toward MVD, respectively, based on study-specific cutoffs. Most identified direct contact with blood and body fluids as an MVD transmission route (92.0%). However, gaps were observed regarding environmental risk factors and MVD distribution and origin. Most recognized reporting suspected cases (91.2%), avoiding contact with infected individuals or their possessions (91.2%), and using personal protective equipment (87.8%). In multivariable analysis, modification of working habits from concern about acquiring MVD (AOR = 2.19, 95% CI: 1.21-3.99) and good MVD knowledge (AOR = 1.96, 95% CI: 1.13-3.39) were positively associated with good practice. Conclusion Findings indicate gaps in MVD-related knowledge and infection prevention among healthcare workers at Dilla University Teaching Hospital. Targeted competency-based training, simulation, IPC resources, and facility-level preparedness systems are warranted to strengthen readiness for MVD and other viral hemorrhagic fever events.

title: An Atlas of Antiviral Therapeutic Outcomes: How Viral Biology Shapes the Reach of Treatment
abstract: Antiviral inhibition does not produce a single therapeutic endpoint: some infections can be cured after finite treatment, others require durable suppression, and others remain difficult to influence because the actionable phase is brief or anatomically inaccessible. These different outcomes reflect the biological state that preserves infection or permits return, the time during which a drug-sensitive process remains causally important, the anatomical space in which consequential virus or viral material resides, and the capacity of viral populations to evolve under therapeutic pressure. Here, we examine these relationships across curable, suppressible, latent, acute, neuroinvasive, and post-acute viral infections. Comparisons among HCV, HIV-1, HBV, HSV, influenza, RSV, dengue, SARS-CoV-2, Ebola virus, CHIKV, and other systems show how persistence architecture, diagnostic timing, tissue pharmacology, host context, and resistance can determine whether antiviral activity translates into virological cure, durable suppression, recurrence control, prevention, or incomplete therapeutic control. Human challenge studies, clinical programs with discordant outcomes, and resistance studies further illustrate where mechanistic activity and therapeutic sufficiency diverge. Across these examples, antiviral outcome depends ultimately on whether treatment can intercept the biological state that determines the subsequent fate of infection.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores how viral biology influences antiviral therapeutic outcomes, emphasizing the variability in treatment success across different viral infections. By comparing systems such as HCV, HIV-1, HBV, HSV, influenza, RSV, dengue, SARS-CoV-2, Ebola virus, and CHIKV, the authors highlight the role of persistence architecture, diagnostic timing, tissue pharmacology, host context, and resistance in determining treatment efficacy. The study suggests that antiviral outcomes depend on whether treatment can intercept the biological state that dictates the fate of infection, offering a novel framework for understanding therapeutic success. However, the analysis is based on abstract-level comparisons and lacks detailed experimental data, limiting the confidence in its conclusions. The findings have implications for the development of targeted antiviral strategies, particularly in the context of Ebola virus disease, by underscoring the importance of viral biology in treatment outcomes.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探索病毒生物学如何影响 抗病毒药物 治疗结果,强调 治疗 在不同病毒感染中成功的差异。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究检查了 埃博拉病毒病 在可治愈、可抑制、潜伏、急性、神经侵袭性和急性后病毒感染方面的结果,包括 埃博拉病毒病 和相关病症。
elements_zh.methods: 作者对包括 埃博拉病毒 在内的各种病毒系统的 抗病毒药物 治疗结果进行了比较分析,以了解影响 治疗 疗效的因素。

title_zh: 抗病毒药物 治疗结果图集:病毒生物学如何影响 治疗 的影响范围
source_body_en: Antiviral inhibition does not produce a single therapeutic endpoint: some infections can be cured after finite treatment, others require durable suppression, and others remain difficult to influence because the actionable phase is brief or anatomically inaccessible. These different outcomes reflect the biological state that preserves infection or permits return, the time during which a drug-sensitive process remains causally important, the anatomical space in which consequential virus or viral material resides, and the capacity of viral populations to evolve under therapeutic pressure. Here, we examine these relationships across curable, suppressible, latent, acute, neuroinvasive, and post-acute viral infections. Comparisons among HCV, HIV-1, HBV, HSV, influenza, RSV, dengue, SARS-CoV-2, Ebola virus, CHIKV, and other systems show how persistence architecture, diagnostic timing, tissue pharmacology, host context, and resistance can determine whether antiviral activity translates into virological cure, durable suppression, recurrence control, prevention, or incomplete therapeutic control. Human challenge studies, clinical programs with discordant outcomes, and resistance studies further illustrate where mechanistic activity and therapeutic sufficiency diverge. Across these examples, antiviral outcome depends ultimately on whether treatment can intercept the biological state that determines the subsequent fate of infection.
abstract_zh: 抗病毒药物 抑制不会产生单一的治疗终点:一些感染可以在有限的 治疗 后治愈,另一些感染需要持久抑制,而另一些感染仍然难以影响,因为可操作阶段短暂或在解剖学上难以接近。这些不同的结果反映了保持感染或允许复发的生物学状态、药物敏感过程仍然具有因果重要性的时间、相应病毒或病毒物质驻留的解剖空间以及病毒群体在治疗压力下进化的能力。在这里,我们研究了可治愈、可抑制、潜伏、急性、神经侵袭性和急性后病毒感染之间的关系。HCV、HIV-1、HBV、HSV、流感、RSV、登革热、SARS-CoV-2、埃博拉病毒、CHIKV 和其他系统之间的比较显示持久性架构、诊断时机、组织药理学、宿主 背景和耐药性如何决定 抗病毒药物 活性是否转化为病毒学治愈、持久抑制、复发控制、预防或不完全治疗控制。人类挑战研究、结果不一致的临床项目以及耐药性研究进一步说明了机械活性和治疗充分性之间的分歧。在这些例子中,抗病毒药物 的结果最终取决于 治疗 是否能够拦截决定感染后续命运的生物状态。

title: A bivalent Lassa virus mRNA vaccine protects guinea pigs from lethal infection with Lassa virus
abstract: Lassa virus (LASV), the causative agent of the life-threatening febrile disease, Lassa fever, remains a major public health concern in West Africa, where hundreds of thousands of infections occur annually. However, no licensed vaccine is currently available, highlighting the urgent need for effective preventive measures. We previously demonstrated that an mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccine expressing LASV glycoprotein precursor (GPC; LASgpc-mRNA-LNP) conferred protection against lethal infection with a recombinant lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus expressing LASV GPC in mice. In this study, we extended our previous work with the aim of evaluating the efficacy of an mRNA-LNP vaccine expressing LASV nucleoprotein (NP; LASnp-mRNA-LNP) and a bivalent vaccine combining LASgpc-mRNA-LNP and LASnp-mRNA-LNP. Using a lethal CBA/N mouse model of infection with ML29, an LASV live-attenuated vaccine candidate encoding LASV GPC and NP, we found that LASgpc-mRNA-LNP and LASnp-mRNA-LNP each conferred protection in the absence of detectable neutralizing antibody responses. We identified LASV GPC- and NP-derived CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell epitope peptides in CBA/N mice and demonstrated that vaccination induced robust antigen-specific T-cell responses. Importantly, the bivalent vaccine provided complete protection against lethal challenge with doses at which monovalent vaccines failed to protect all mice, suggesting a potential dose-sparing benefit of the bivalent formulation. Furthermore, the bivalent vaccine fully protected guinea pigs against lethal challenge with authentic LASV. Together, these findings establish LASV NP, in addition to GPC, as a protective antigen in the mRNA vaccine platform and provide a rationale for developing bivalent mRNA-LNP vaccines to improve protection against Lassa fever.

title: Beyond long COVID: post-acute infection syndromes across Africa, a systematic review
abstract: Post-acute infection syndromes (PAIS) have gained global attention through Long COVID, yet many pathogens most closely linked to PAIS are endemic to Africa, where evidence remains scarce; a gap with implications for health equity and global health security. We aimed to systematically review the prevalence, clinical presentation, and associated factors of PAIS following non-COVID infections in Africa, and to identify priorities for future research. We conducted a systematic review, searching Medline, Embase, and grey literature until 7 November 2025 for studies in Africa reporting symptoms four or more weeks after acute infection. Case reports, case series, conference abstracts, secondary research, comments, and correspondence were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data on study characteristics, symptom prevalence, clinical presentation, and associated factors. As substantial heterogeneity was observed across studies, results were summarised descriptively. The study was registered on the Open Science Framework. Of 1,368 records, 65 studies were included, 42 on Ebola virus disease and 19 on chikungunya, with moderate to low risk of bias. Prevalence of PAIS ranged from 17.5% to 98.6% after Ebola and 12.1% to 78.6% after chikungunya. Musculoskeletal pain, ocular complications, headache, and fatigue predominated after Ebola; arthralgia was the hallmark of post-chikungunya disease. Substantial symptom burden persisted years after acute infection. Female sex, older age, and greater acute disease severity were the factors most frequently reported to be associated with persistent sequelae. An exploratory, non-systematic supplementary search additionally identified sex-specific consequences among female survivors including menstrual irregularities and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Despite scarce, heterogeneous, and geographically concentrated evidence, the reported prevalence of persistent symptoms among survivors is high, although the absence of comparison groups in most studies complicates attribution to the infection itself. Health systems in Africa must adapt to provide long-term survivor care, embedding follow-up into existing chronic care platforms. As pathogens endemic to Africa carry pandemic potential and expand geographically, understanding their chronic consequences is both a matter of health equity and an urgent global health security priority.

analysis.summary_en: This study systematically reviews post-acute infection syndromes (PAIS) following non-COVID infections in Africa, focusing on Ebola virus disease and chikungunya. It highlights the high prevalence of persistent symptoms, such as musculoskeletal pain, ocular complications, headache, and fatigue after Ebola, and arthralgia after chikungunya. The research underscores the need for long-term survivor care and identifies factors like female sex, older age, and greater acute disease severity as associated with persistent sequelae. The study's limitations include the descriptive summarization of results due to substantial heterogeneity across studies, and the absence of comparison groups in most studies complicates the attribution of symptoms to the infection itself. The findings emphasize the importance of understanding the chronic consequences of pathogens endemic to Africa, which have pandemic potential and expand geographically, as a matter of health equity and global health security.

title_zh: 超越长期新冠疫情:非洲急性感染后综合症的系统评价
source_body_en: Post-acute infection syndromes (PAIS) have gained global attention through Long COVID, yet many pathogens most closely linked to PAIS are endemic to Africa, where evidence remains scarce; a gap with implications for health equity and global health security. We aimed to systematically review the prevalence, clinical presentation, and associated factors of PAIS following non-COVID infections in Africa, and to identify priorities for future research. We conducted a systematic review, searching Medline, Embase, and grey literature until 7 November 2025 for studies in Africa reporting symptoms four or more weeks after acute infection. Case reports, case series, conference abstracts, secondary research, comments, and correspondence were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data on study characteristics, symptom prevalence, clinical presentation, and associated factors. As substantial heterogeneity was observed across studies, results were summarised descriptively. The study was registered on the Open Science Framework. Of 1,368 records, 65 studies were included, 42 on Ebola virus disease and 19 on chikungunya, with moderate to low risk of bias. Prevalence of PAIS ranged from 17.5% to 98.6% after Ebola and 12.1% to 78.6% after chikungunya. Musculoskeletal pain, ocular complications, headache, and fatigue predominated after Ebola; arthralgia was the hallmark of post-chikungunya disease. Substantial symptom burden persisted years after acute infection. Female sex, older age, and greater acute disease severity were the factors most frequently reported to be associated with persistent sequelae. An exploratory, non-systematic supplementary search additionally identified sex-specific consequences among female survivors including menstrual irregularities and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Despite scarce, heterogeneous, and geographically concentrated evidence, the reported prevalence of persistent symptoms among survivors is high, although the absence of comparison groups in most studies complicates attribution to the infection itself. Health systems in Africa must adapt to provide long-term survivor care, embedding follow-up into existing chronic care platforms. As pathogens endemic to Africa carry pandemic potential and expand geographically, understanding their chronic consequences is both a matter of health equity and an urgent global health security priority.
abstract_zh: 急性感染后综合症(PAIS)通过长新冠病毒引起了全球关注,但许多与 PAIS 密切相关的病原体是非洲流行的,而那里的证据仍然匮乏;这一差距对卫生公平和全球卫生安全产生影响。我们的目的是系统地回顾非洲非新冠病毒感染后 PAIS 的 患病率、临床表现和相关因素,并确定未来研究的重点。我们进行了系统回顾,检索了截至 2025 年 11 月 7 日的 Medline、Embase 和灰色文献,寻找在非洲报告急性感染后四周或更长时间出现症状的研究。病例报告、案例系列、会议摘要、二次研究、评论和信件被排除在外。两名评审员独立筛选记录并提取有关研究特征、症状 患病率、临床表现和相关因素的数据。由于研究中观察到显着的异质性,因此对结果进行了描述性总结。该研究已在开放科学框架上注册。在 1,368 条记录中,纳入了 65 项研究,其中 42 项涉及 埃博拉病毒病,19 项涉及基孔肯雅热,具有中度至低度偏倚风险。埃博拉病毒后 PAIS 的 患病率 范围为 17.5% 至 98.6%,基孔肯雅热病毒后 PAIS 范围为 12.1% 至 78.6%。埃博拉病毒感染后主要表现为肌肉骨骼疼痛、眼部并发症、头痛和疲劳;关节痛是后基孔肯雅病的标志。严重的症状负担在急性感染后持续数年。女性、年龄较大和急性疾病严重程度是最常报告的与持续性后遗症相关的因素。一项探索性的、非系统性的补充搜索还发现了女性幸存者中特定性别的后果,包括月经不调和不良妊娠结局。尽管证据稀缺、异质且地理集中,但报告的幸存者中持续症状的 患病率 很高,尽管大多数研究中缺乏对照组使感染本身的归因变得复杂。非洲的卫生系统必须适应提供长期幸存者护理,将后续行动纳入现有的慢性病护理平台。由于非洲流行的病原体具有大流行的可能性并在地理上扩大,了解其长期后果既是卫生公平问题,也是全球卫生安全的紧迫优先事项。

title: Immunoinformatics and reverse vaccinology design of self-amplifying RNA vaccine against marburg virus with structural dynamics and immune simulation analysis
abstract: Marburg virus disease (MVD), a deadly zoonotic illness in humans, is caused by the Marburg virus (MARV), a single-stranded RNA virus belonging to the Orthomarburgvirus genus of the Filoviridae family. There are currently no approved vaccines or efficient antiviral therapies for MARV, despite high morbidity and fatality rates of the virus, particularly in Africa. Recognizing its epidemic potential and its inclusion on the WHO list of blueprint priority pathogens, an immunoinformatics approach was used to design novel multi-epitope saRNA vaccine candidates (MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII) targeting the viral GP, NP, VP40, and VP35 via CD8 + , CD4 + , and B cell epitopes. These epitopes were derived from target protein sequences and incorporated into MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII after validation for antigenicity, non-allergenicity, non-toxicity, and conservation. Additionally, the selected epitopes were conjugated to suitable adjuvants via various linkers, thereby enabling the design of a potentially stable vaccine. Additionally, the designed MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII were incorporated into the standard saRNA model, in which ORF-2 encodes the target vaccine peptide. Moreover, biophysical analyses unveiled that the developed vaccines are basic (pI < 7), soluble (GRAVY < 0), and stable (aliphatic index < 80). Subsequently, docking of MB-saVaxI to TLR2 (-938.3) and TLR4 (-902.4), and MB-saVaxII to TLR3 (-1485.4) and TLR7 (-1543.6) demonstrated significant affinity, with detailed hydrogen-bond interactions validated by MM-GBSA and molecular dynamics simulations. Furthermore, MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII were effectively cloned in-silico into Escherichia coli, and immune simulations indicated that the vaccines triggered robust innate and adaptive immunity, with a sustained memory response and TH cell activation, as evidenced by IFN-γ and IL-2 production. Additionally, the mRNA structure of MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII remained stable throughout the expression pathway in the host. However, extensive in-vitro and in-vivo studies are needed to establish the safety and efficacy of this vaccine candidate conclusively.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study highlights the need for effective vaccines against Bundibugyo virus due to its potential to cause severe disease and the lack of existing therapeutic options. The objective is to explore vaccine development possibilities for this virus.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This editorial discusses the research landscape surrounding vaccines for Bundibugyo virus, focusing on the potential of existing vaccine platforms and their application to this specific virus. The study is based on a review of available literature and expert opinion.
analysis.methods: The editorial reviews existing vaccine research and evaluates the potential of vaccine platforms developed for other Ebola viruses, such as Sudan virus and Zaire ebolavirus, to be adapted for Bundibugyo virus. It does not describe specific experimental methods or statistical analyses.
analysis.main_results: The editorial reports that preliminary studies suggest the possibility of using vaccine platforms developed for other Ebola viruses to create efficacious vaccines for Bundibugyo virus. However, no specific results or data are provided in the text.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as a promising avenue for vaccine development against Bundibugyo virus, noting that existing platforms may be applicable. This represents a novel perspective on the potential for cross-virus vaccine strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that vaccine development for Bundibugyo virus could benefit from leveraging existing platforms, which may inform future research and public health strategies for preventing outbreaks of this virus.

title: Bundibugyo virus disease in outbreak settings: A practical clinical review
abstract: Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) is a severe filovirus infection caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), an orthoebolavirus with diagnostic and countermeasure implications distinct from Ebola virus (EBOV). The ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has expanded substantially, with 7890 confirmed cases and 3799 deaths reported across 63 health zones in seven provinces as of 23 September 2026. BVD usually presents as a nonspecific febrile and gastrointestinal illness; haemorrhagic manifestations are uncommon at presentation. Early outbreak investigation also showed that EBOV-oriented testing can fail to detect BDBV, making species-appropriate molecular testing essential when BDBV is epidemiologically plausible. Supportive care remains the standard of management, but what can be delivered safely differs between peripheral facilities and dedicated filovirus treatment centres. First-contact facilities should prioritise recognition, separation, protected sampling, treatment of immediately life-threatening or common treatable conditions, and early referral; treatment centres can provide closer monitoring, advanced supportive care, and access to approved research protocols. Insecurity, displacement, laboratory and transport constraints, and delayed presentation continue to limit implementation. No vaccine or specific therapeutic has established clinical efficacy against BDBV in humans; Ervebo is being evaluated within research protocols and the PARTNERS trial is evaluating MBP134 and remdesivir-based regimens. This review synthesises historical and current evidence on recognition, diagnosis, clinical care, infection prevention, referral, and emerging countermeasures in outbreak-affected settings.

title_zh: 暴发 环境中的本迪布焦病毒病:实用临床回顾
source_body_en: Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) is a severe filovirus infection caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), an orthoebolavirus with diagnostic and countermeasure implications distinct from Ebola virus (EBOV). The ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has expanded substantially, with 7890 confirmed cases and 3799 deaths reported across 63 health zones in seven provinces as of 23 September 2026. BVD usually presents as a nonspecific febrile and gastrointestinal illness; haemorrhagic manifestations are uncommon at presentation. Early outbreak investigation also showed that EBOV-oriented testing can fail to detect BDBV, making species-appropriate molecular testing essential when BDBV is epidemiologically plausible. Supportive care remains the standard of management, but what can be delivered safely differs between peripheral facilities and dedicated filovirus treatment centres. First-contact facilities should prioritise recognition, separation, protected sampling, treatment of immediately life-threatening or common treatable conditions, and early referral; treatment centres can provide closer monitoring, advanced supportive care, and access to approved research protocols. Insecurity, displacement, laboratory and transport constraints, and delayed presentation continue to limit implementation. No vaccine or specific therapeutic has established clinical efficacy against BDBV in humans; Ervebo is being evaluated within research protocols and the PARTNERS trial is evaluating MBP134 and remdesivir-based regimens. This review synthesises historical and current evidence on recognition, diagnosis, clinical care, infection prevention, referral, and emerging countermeasures in outbreak-affected settings.
